primary.title: Hamlet
primary.author: William Shakespeare
primary.rationale: Considered one of Shakespeare's greatest tragedies, it explores themes of revenge, betrayal, and mortality. Its enduring popularity ensures wide availability.

primary.title: Romeo and Juliet
primary.author: William Shakespeare
primary.rationale: A quintessential tragedy of young love and feuding families, this play is one of Shakespeare's most frequently performed and studied works.

primary.title: Macbeth
primary.author: William Shakespeare
primary.rationale: A dark and powerful tragedy exploring ambition, guilt, and the supernatural, Macbeth is a staple of Shakespearean literature.

secondary.title: Shakespeare: The Invention of the Human
secondary.author: Harold Bloom
secondary.rationale: A highly influential and comprehensive critical analysis of Shakespeare's plays and their impact on Western literature and thought.

secondary.title: The Cambridge Companion to Shakespeare
secondary.author: Harold Bloom
secondary.rationale: A collection of essays by leading scholars offering diverse perspectives on Shakespeare's life, works, and historical context.

secondary.title: Shakespeare's Tragedies: A History of the Tragic Form
secondary.author: John P. Brockington
secondary.rationale: Examines the evolution of the tragic form in Shakespeare's plays, providing scholarly analysis of key works and their dramatic conventions.

suggestions.notes: Shakespeare's primary sources are his plays and poems. Secondary sources provide critical analysis and historical context.
